title: Eid Celebration
strapline: New clothes, a special feast, henna patterns and 'Eid Mubarak!' — a joyful day of family, sharing and giving.
intent: Eid — both Eid al-Fitr, marking the end of Ramadan, and Eid al-Adha — is a day of joy, family, generosity and feasting for Muslim communities, and its warmth is easy for young children to share.
Celebrating a real festival from families in the community helps every child value their friends' traditions and feel proud and seen when their own are honoured.
Making cards, decorating with lanterns and stars, and creating henna-inspired patterns invites beautiful creative and fine-motor work.
The traditions weave in mathematics — the crescent moon and stars to draw and count, patterns to repeat, gifts and treats to share fairly.
Children build real knowledge of the wider world and language to talk about it — Eid, crescent, moon, feast, celebrate, share, generosity.
Sharing food, giving to others and welcoming everyone to the celebration grows kindness, generosity and belonging.
implementation: Learn about Eid with the families who celebrate it — invite them to share how they mark the day, and follow their lead so it is accurate and respectful.
Offer card-making, crescent-and-star decorations, lantern crafts and henna-inspired pattern-making with paint, pens or loose parts on hands and paper.
Model the greeting and the wonder: 'We say Eid Mubarak, which means Blessed Eid — I wonder what your family does to celebrate.'
Bring in maths through the symbols and sharing — draw and count crescent moons and stars, repeat henna patterns, share treats one to each friend.
Set out a role-play feast where children dress up, welcome guests, prepare and share special foods, and give cards and small gifts.
Share the spirit of generosity — giving to others, welcoming everyone in — and, where safe and with families, taste special foods together.
key_questions: We say Eid Mubarak — I wonder what your family does to celebrate?
How many crescent moons and stars can you count?
What pattern is your henna design making?
Have we got a card and a treat for every friend?
What special food does your family share on Eid?

impact.text: Children value a real festival of family and generosity and feel proud when their own traditions are honoured.
Children make cards, lanterns, stars and henna-inspired patterns — beautiful creative and fine-motor work.
Children draw and count crescent moons and stars and repeat patterns.
Children share treats fairly, one to each friend, and give cards and gifts.
Children grow words for the festival — Eid, crescent, feast, celebrate, share, generosity.

enhancements: A role-play feast where children dress up, welcome guests and share special foods.
Crescent-and-star decorations and lantern crafts to hang and display.
Henna-inspired pattern-making with paint, pens or loose parts on hands and paper.
Families invited to share how they mark the day, following their lead.
Cards and small gifts to make and give in the spirit of generosity.

playing_exploring: Children step into the joy, colour and feasting of a real festival, bringing their own family experiences to the play.
They make, decorate and pattern with paint, paper and loose parts.
active_learning: Children prepare and host the celebration together, seeing the feast, the cards and the welcome through.
creating_thinking: Children repeat and invent henna and decoration patterns and make sense of a festival alongside their own.
